source.analysis_execution: Docker, network disabled, read-only evidence mount, user 0, CPU 0.25, memory 128 MiB

measurement_contract.quantiles: nearest rank, with P50 and P95 computed over each metric's own observed sample
measurement_contract.origin: first persisted event received_at; all 33 equal expert message created_at in this snapshot
measurement_contract.first_acceptance: timestamp of first successful mcp_record_expert_signals trace carrying a non-empty accepted list, minus first persisted event timestamp
measurement_contract.last_acceptance: timestamp of last successful mcp_record_expert_signals trace carrying a non-empty accepted list, minus first persisted event timestamp
measurement_contract.acceptance_commit_caveat: A trace timestamp is inside the tool transaction, not an observed COMMIT. Reported acceptance delays are approximations and may understate externally visible commit delay.
measurement_contract.conclusion: system_review_result.payload.event_to_conclusion_ms; this is later than initial accepted recommendation and must not replace that metric
measurement_contract.concurrency: half-open claim trace to final conclusion trace intervals, or job updated_at when a conclusion is absent; does not include post-conclusion session cleanup
measurement_contract.misses_are_not_successes: An unresolved or timed-out message does not count as successful identification within 20 seconds. Nine accepted signals are a selected success sample, not all 33 messages.

observed_concurrency.interpretation: This window proves four review intervals can overlap and at least two reviews for one expert can overlap. It does not prove unlimited capacity, absence of all contention, or a strict 20-second guarantee. No historical replay lane was claimed in this window.

accepted_outliers.explanation: A 14.106-second queue delay consumed most of the end-to-end budget before the model started.
The first round returned without verified completion after searches and resolution. A correctness continuation added another model round. Fast database tools did not dominate the elapsed time.
Large intervals between fast tool calls indicate model/provider round-trip time dominates this accepted recommendation.

conclusions: The observed window violates 20 seconds even when the later persistence origin is used: at least 3 of 9 accepted recommendations were late.
The original detection timestamp is absent, so this window cannot establish the true detection-to-recommendation distribution.
Current tool SQL latency and media input preparation do not explain the largest delays in this window; avoid broad database rewrites based on older remote-database reports.
Do not relax complete search, unique identity, phase, period, line, current price or trusted-source checks to reduce latency.
A shared absolute API write fence prevents late signals, but timeouts remain unresolved failures of the success SLA and must be reported separately.
